definitions.standard: A stable subatomic particle with a charge of negative electricity, found in all atoms and acting as the primary carrier of electricity in solids.
definitions.simple: A tiny, invisible particle zooming around the outside of an atom. It has a negative charge and makes electricity work!
definitions.scientific: A subatomic particle of matter that is bound to the nucleus by electromagnetic forces. It has a rest mass of 9.109 × 10⁻³¹ kilograms and a negative elementary charge.

linguistics.origin: Coined in 1891 by George Johnstone Stoney from 'electric' + '-on'.

examples: Flow of electrons in a copper wire

advanced_data.history: Discovered by J.J. Thomson in 1897 using a cathode ray tube.

common_misconceptions: Electrons crash into the nucleus. (They don't, because they occupy specific discrete energy levels).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Think of electrons like race cars on a track around a stadium. They have to stay on their specific track!
